question.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

I. Any $4\times 3$ matrix $A$ has at most $3$ distinct singular values.

II. The singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}]$ are non-negative.

III. Any $3\times 4$ matrix $A$ has at most $3$ distinct singular values.
question.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

- Statement I is true. Since $A$ is a $4\times 3$ matrix and ${A}^{T}$ is a $3\times 4$ matrix, ${A}^{T}\,A$ must be a $3\times 3$ matrix: 

$$
{{A}^{T}}_{3\times 4}\times {A}_{4\times 3}={{A}^{T}\,A}_{3\times 3}
$$

Hence, $A$ has at most $3$ distinct singular values.

- Statement II is true. All singular values of any matrix are non-negative.

- Statement III is false. Since $A$ is a $3\times 4$ matrix and ${A}^{T}$ is a $4\times 3$ matrix, ${A}^{T}\,A$ must be a $4\times 4$ matrix: 

$$
{{A}^{T}}_{4\times 3}\times {A}_{3\times 4}={{A}^{T}\,A}_{4\times 4}
$$

Hence, $A$ has at most $4$ distinct singular values.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
